examples.scenario: An int16 minimum of -32000 and maximum of 32000 are passed directly to peak-to-peak
examples.reason: The true difference exceeds int16 and can wrap to a negative result.

examples.scenario: Unsigned values are subtracted in the wrong order and wrap to a large positive number
examples.reason: Unsigned arithmetic cannot represent a negative diagnostic difference.

examples.scenario: Minimum and maximum have equal numbers but one is metres and the other is feet
examples.reason: Numerical subtraction is meaningless until units and vertical reference agree.

examples.scenario: A caller reports absolute value without proving which operand is the maximum
examples.reason: Absolute value can hide reversed or mislabeled extrema.
Equivalent zero results should have one canonical serialized representation.

examples.scenario: Four minimum ties and three maximum ties exist
examples.reason: Every valid extrema pairing must remain auditable even though the numeric difference is equal.

examples.scenario: Parallel workers emit tied pairs in completion order
examples.reason: Pair identity must not depend on worker timing.

examples.scenario: The result changes by one adjacent representable float after a library change
examples.reason: A one-ULP difference is detectable but is not evidence of source accuracy.
